answer: The time keeper fills every hourglass from one dune and logs the calibration, and no caravan may set out until the glasses agree on the hour. A jade glass filled from another dune fails the log: at the thread of the sand the grains must fall at the rate the keeper recorded, and a strange glass strands the caravan at noon. Forging the calibration means keeping the glasses for a year, calibrating 120 of them and paying 5,800, while the basalt entry in the time keeper's log is read before every departure, so a glass whose calibration never happened is smashed.
